    Content from 1. Introduction to genetic variation and variant calling

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 50 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • What kinds of genetic variation can short-read sequencing detect?
    • How does a variant caller turn aligned reads into a genotype?
    • Why can a variant call be wrong?
    • What question will we answer with the Ashkenazi trio today?

    Objectives

    • Distinguish SNVs, MNVs, indels and SVs/CNVs, and germline from somatic variants.
    • Read diploid genotypes (0/0, 0/1, 1/1, ./.).
    • Explain how a call is inferred from read evidence and base and mapping quality, and why errors arise.
    • Describe the workflow and its files.
    • State the workshop question for the GIAB Ashkenazi trio (HG002, HG003, HG004).

    Stub: content arrives in phase P4.

    Content from 2. Data, reference genomes, and project setup

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 40 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • What data will we analyze, and where does it come from?
    • What makes a reference genome suitable for variant calling?
    • How do we organize the project and record sample metadata?
    • How do we check that the data is complete and unchanged?

    Objectives

    • Verify the staged copy and lay out the project.
    • Describe the HG002, HG003 and HG004 trio and record its metadata as a sample sheet and a PED file.
    • Explain the GRCh38 no-alt analysis set, contig naming and index files (.fai, .dict, aligner index).
    • Convert BED (0-based, half-open) to VCF-style (1-based) coordinates.
    • Check integrity with md5.

    Stub: content arrives in phase P4.

    Content from 3. Read quality control

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 30 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • How do we tell whether the sequencing reads are good enough to call variants?
    • Do these reads need trimming before alignment?

    Objectives

    • Run FastQC and MultiQC in an interactive job.
    • Interpret base quality, adapter content, duplication and GC.
    • Decide whether trimming is needed before local alignment.

    Content from 4. Read alignment and alignment QC

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 90 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • How are reads placed on the reference genome?
    • Why does mapping quality matter for variant calling?
    • How do we produce analysis-ready BAM files on the cluster?
    • How do we know the alignment worked?

    Objectives

    • Explain why mapping quality matters for calling.
    • Align with bwa mem using correct read groups.
    • Produce sorted, duplicate-marked and indexed BAMs.
    • Read SAM fields (FLAG, CIGAR, MAPQ).
    • Interpret mapping, pairing, duplicate, insert-size and coverage metrics.
    • View a locus.

    Content from 5A. Calling variants with bcftools

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 60 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • How does bcftools turn aligned reads into genotype calls?
    • Why call the trio jointly?
    • How do we read a VCF record?

    Objectives

    • Explain what mpileup summarizes and how call turns it into genotypes and QUAL.
    • Call the trio jointly by region with an array job.
    • Concatenate, normalize (left-align, split multiallelic sites) and index the calls.
    • Read a VCF record (REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER, INFO; GT, GQ, PL, AD, DP).

    Stub: content arrives in phase P5.

    Content from 6. Filtering and evaluating variant calls

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 80 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • How do we summarize a call set?
    • How do we choose and apply filters?
    • How good are our calls, and how do we know?
    • What can we measure when there is no truth set?

    Objectives

    • Summarize a call set (counts, Ts/Tv, het/hom-alt ratio, indel lengths, depth and QUAL distributions).
    • Apply soft filters at the site and genotype levels.
    • Measure precision and recall against a GIAB benchmark in its confident regions.
    • Explain the precision-recall trade-off of a threshold and why indels and difficult regions do worse.
    • Choose proxy measures when no truth set exists.

    Stub: content arrives in phase P5.

    Content from 7. Annotating variants

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 60 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • What does a variant do to a gene or protein?
    • How common is a variant in the population?
    • What are the limits of annotation?

    Objectives

    • Annotate consequences with SnpEff using a database that matches the reference build.
    • Add gnomAD allele frequencies, including the ancestry-matched group.
    • Read ANN fields (allele, effect, impact, gene, transcript, HGVS).
    • Filter and tabulate by impact and frequency.
    • Explain annotation caveats.

    Stub: content arrives in phase P6.

    Content from 8. Application: candidate variants in a family trio

    Last updated on 2026-10-09 | Edit this page

    Estimated time: 75 minutes

    Overview

    Questions

    • Which variants in HG002 are consistent with a de novo or recessive model?
    • How many candidates survive quality, annotation and frequency filters?
    • What does the evidence support, and what does it not?

    Objectives

    • Confirm relationships and sample order before trio analysis.
    • Report the Mendelian-consistency rate as a QC metric.
    • Select de novo and recessive candidates with genotype expressions.
    • Add quality and annotation filters and report a filtering funnel.
    • Inspect candidates in IGV and against the benchmark.
    • Write an interpretation that separates call quality from biological significance.

    Stub: content arrives in phase P6.
